summary: Alfred Hillebrandt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Martin Haug. He held associate and full professorships at the University of Breslau between 1883 and 1902.

Alfred Körte worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studying at the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig University between circa 1895 and 1934.

Indologist and linguist Alfred Ludwig studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under scholars including Albrecht Weber. He qualified at Vienna in 1858 and served as a professor at Charles University from 1860 to 1871.

Alfred Métraux studied around 1925–1928 at the École des chartes, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Marcel Mauss. He later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1959 to 1963.

Ali S. Asani specializes in religious studies and Indology. He completed his undergraduate and graduate education at Harvard College and Harvard University between circa 1973 and 1984, subsequently becoming a professor of Middle Eastern and Indo-Muslim studies there from 1983.
Alice Y. Tseng, a scholar of Japanology and history and archaeology, studied as a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang. She is attested as a professor at Boston University in 2013.

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under supervisors Steven Collins and Bruce Lincoln, also studying under Saw Tun, Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, as well as instructors Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held professorships at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and the University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. He served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College, attested in 2001.

Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Vighnahari Bhalacandra Deo, R. Srinivasan Raghavachariar, and K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. He later worked at the Library of Congress from circa 1985 to 2016.
Allison Busch was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She held an appointment as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University, attested for 2026.

Alnis Dickson, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed an MA at McGill University, attested in 2009. His studies were supervised by Lara Braitstein, and he was taught by G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a PhD at Würzburg and studied with Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Lucknow State Museum, and the Archaeological Survey of India.

Alois Müller was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. Between 1867 and 1879, he held posts at Vienna University Library and Palacký University Olomouc, before becoming director of Graz University Library in 1879.

Aloysius Pieris, a religious and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from London, Sri Lanka, and Tilburg, among other institutions. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre from 1974 and held visiting chairs at several theological institutes.
Alubomulle Sumanasara is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University from circa 1980 to 1988 under the supervision of Yasuaki Nara.

Indologist Alvappillai Veluppillai earned doctorates from the University of Ceylon under K. Kanapathypillai and Oxford under Thomas Burrow. He held academic posts at Ceylon, Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala, and Arizona State University, among others.

Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1968 and was later a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied as a doctoral student under T. R. V. Murti and also studied under Michel Hulin.
